prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell) coordinates Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport; integrates regional flow management/Airport Collaborative Decision-Making. Elements: Demand Prediction Service/Capacity Assessment Module/Slot Allocation Engine/Airport CDM Portal/Digital Briefing Room/Tower Sequence Manager/Ramp Movement Board/Departure Metering Service/Arrival Regulation Console/Contingency Operations Console/Weather Ingest Gateway/Flight Data Exchange/Surface Surveillance Adapter/Airline Interface Adapter/Alert Distribution Hub/Performance Analytics Warehouse/Audit Event Ledger/Identity Access Service/Business Rules Registry/Time Synchronization Service/Common Situation Display. Indicators: North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter/East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor/Sector Load Monitor/Gate Conflict Detector. Modes: Normal Operations/Adverse Weather Mode/Capacity Reduction State/Recovery Phase/Contingency Fallback State/Slot Compliance State.
Regional Flow Manager (Copperfin) owns intent/horizon/cutover/checkpoints; aligns demand/capacity/milestones; reviews Airport Capacity Plan/Ground Delay Program/Tactical Regulation Proposal before agreement. Airspace Sector Planner validates sector constraints/smoothing; Military Airspace Liaison confirms assumptions. Slot Coordinator owns Calculated Takeoff Time policy; verifies engine’s registry parameters. Airline Operations Coordinator ensures complete/timely/traceable Flight Intent Message updates; Aircraft Operator Representative supplies aircraft constraints/achievable portal commitments. Network Operations Liaison ensures adjacent-network compatibility; records outcomes in Collaborative Decision Log. Meteorology Briefing Officer produces Storm Cell Snapshot before review; briefs gateway forecasts/uncertainty/mode-transition triggers. Airport Duty Manager owns escalation/portal-display consistency. Tower Supervisor sends Runway Inspection Note; owns sequencing/current configuration. Ramp Control Lead maintains board/metering reliability. Ground Handling Dispatcher verifies Handling Resource Planner assumptions; escalates deviations. Other actors: Deicing Coordinator/Emergency Response Coordinator/Data Governance Steward/System Support Engineer.
Exchange normalizes intents/schedules; prediction produces demand; gateway preserves issue-times. Capacity module combines declarations/weather/airspace/stands/resources into demand-tested Airport Acceptance Rate. Metering estimates provisional Target Off Block Time sensitivity; arrival console highlights interventions. Briefing displays plan/logs assumptions; situation display shares approved baseline; alerts announce changes; warehouse retains evidence. Morning baseline precedes bank-locking. Reduced capacity requires rapid proposal/consistent delay program; recovery monitors off-block/takeoff-time compliance.

New part:
S092: The Deicing Coordinator provides pre-tactical and tactical advice when winter operations affect departure readiness, metering stability, or achievable throughput.
S093: The Military Airspace Liaison confirms military airspace availability assumptions and alerts the Regional Flow Manager when civil routing options may be constrained.
S094: During tactical operations, the Regional Flow Manager chairs decision checkpoints and authorizes changes to flow measures when the Capacity Assessment Module indicates that declared capacity no longer matches observed conditions.
S095: The Departure Metering Service and Arrival Regulation Console are used only under the authority of the accountable flow roles, and their outputs must remain visible on the Common Situation Display.
S096: Escalation to the Emergency Response Coordinator is required when a safety event, security event, or emergency response activity may affect airport acceptance, surface movement, or airspace availability.
S097: The System Support Engineer is the technical escalation contact for degraded Regional Flow Platform functions, interface outages, or abnormal behavior in the Flight Data Exchange.
S098: The Data Governance Steward verifies that operational decisions, role acknowledgements, and exception handling are captured in the Audit Event Ledger with synchronized timestamps from the Time Synchronization Service.
S099: At the end of each tactical period, accountable roles confirm that decisions and unresolved issues are available to the Performance Analytics Warehouse for later inclusion in the Post Operations Report.
S100: The capacity picture is built from demand forecasts, observed traffic, airport resource status, airspace constraints, and weather products that are updated throughout the tactical planning horizon.
S101: The Demand Prediction Service, also known as Marlinstone, generates the demand forecast used by the Regional Flow Platform.
S102: The Weather Ingest Gateway, also known as Orchard, normalizes external and local meteorological feeds before they are used in operational capacity calculations.
S103: The Demand Prediction Service receives filed flight information through the Flight Data Exchange and compares it with the current operating schedule held by the Airline Interface Adapter.
S104: Flight Intent Message updates are treated as the primary indicator of operator intent when the system detects a material difference from the published schedule.
S105: The Demand Prediction Service uses recent conformance history, aircraft rotation timing, and known bank structures to estimate arrival and departure loads by planning interval.
S106: The Sector Load Monitor contributes airspace demand indicators so that airport capacity is not assessed independently of nearby sector saturation.
S107: The Capacity Assessment Module combines demand projections with the Airport Capacity Plan to determine whether a published Airport Acceptance Rate remains feasible.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
